Recipe parameters: placeholders, binding and merging

Source: R/merge_v2.R, R/params_v2.R
omop_param.Rd

omop_param() declares a named placeholder of a fixed type that may stand for a value in any language-2 constructor (an event's concepts, a window bound, an era gap, a matching seed, a predicate literal inside omop_where, ...). The same name may appear several times; every occurrence must carry the same definition.

Usage

recipe_merge(a, b, prefix = NULL)

omop_param(
  name,
  type = c("concept_set", "event", "integer", "number", "string", "date", "window"),
  default = NULL,
  description = NULL
)

recipe_params(recipe)

recipe_bind(recipe, ...)

Arguments

a, b

Recipes to merge (recipe_merge()).

prefix

NULL (one shared namespace) or a name: every node of b is renamed <prefix>_<name> and every reference to it is rewritten.

name

Parameter name (a letter, then letters, digits or underscores).

type

Parameter type (see Details).

default

Optional default value of the declared type; NULL leaves the parameter unbound until recipe_bind().

description

Optional description.

recipe

An omop_recipe.

...

recipe_bind(): values by parameter name (name = value).

Value

omop_param(): a parameter placeholder. recipe_params(): a named list of the declared parameters, in order of first appearance. recipe_bind(): the bound recipe.

Details

recipe_merge(a, b, prefix = NULL) joins two recipes. Without a prefix both share one namespace: a name used by both must carry the same definition, and their base populations, recipe-level filters, scopes, plan options and coverage defaults must agree. With a prefix every node of b (concept sets, events, intervals, populations, variables, blocks, outputs) is renamed and every reference rewritten – anchors, censoring (and its when_index_source tags), index arms, parents, set-operation members, match inputs, output rows and columns, output dependencies and publication roots; b's base population keeps its meaning (its recipe-level filters move onto it) and is shared only when it equals a's. When equality depends on parameters, it is reconsidered after binding or default resolution against the current population and source definitions, preserving edits made after merging. Outputs whose columns were implicit (every variable) are made explicit first, so each output keeps exactly its own variables. Block metadata (block_id, block_version) is preserved. Parameters are shared by name.

recipe_params() lists the parameters a recipe declares. recipe_bind() binds values by name: each value is checked against the declared type and substituted, and every object that held a placeholder is rebuilt through its constructor, so a bound recipe is validated exactly like a hand-written one. Parameters left unbound keep their placeholder (a recipe may be bound in stages). recipe_to_plan binds the remaining parameters to their defaults and refuses a parameter without a default.

Integer and number parameters admit the arithmetic operators +, -, * and / (also unary minus and unary plus) with numeric literals and other numeric parameters, e.g. omop_window(-omop_param("washout", type = "integer"), -1); the expression is evaluated when its parameters are bound and its value is then validated where it is used.

Types and the values they accept: "integer" (an exact integer), "number" (a finite number), "string" (one string), "date" (an ISO date or a Date), "concept_set" (an omop_concept_set, concept IDs, or the name of a registry concept set), "event" (an omop_event, an omop_era, or the name of a declared one) and "window" (an omop_window).

See also

recipe_merge, recipe_to_plan

Examples

rec <- omop_recipe(
  populations = list(omop_population("c1", index = omop_index(
    list(cohort_definition_id = omop_param("cohort", type = "integer", default = 1)),
    select = "all"))),
  variables = list(dm = omop_variable(
    event = omop_event("condition_occurrence", omop_param("dx", type = "concept_set")),
    reducer = omop_reduce("binary", window = omop_window(-omop_param("lookback",
      type = "integer", default = 365L), 0)))),
  outputs = list(omop_output("w", rows = "c1", format = "wide")))
names(recipe_params(rec))
bound <- recipe_bind(rec, dx = omop_concept_set(201820, descendants = TRUE))
